Event: US tariff measures linked to Russian oil purchases
Key actors: Government of India; United States government
What happened?: India said new US tariff measures targeting countries purchasing Russian oil could affect bilateral relations and stated that it would protect its energy security.
Why does it matter?: The development links India's relations with the United States, Russian energy imports, trade exposure and energy security.

Event: Nationwide protests over voter-roll changes
Key actors: Election Commission of India; Congress party; protesters; police
What happened?: Police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse opposition protesters during nationwide demonstrations demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over allegations of voter-roll manipulation.
Why does it matter?: The protests and police response indicate increased public and political contestation around the electoral-roll verification process and the Election Commission.

Event: India-China military talks amid tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
Key actors: Indian Army; Chinese military; Ministry of External Affairs
What happened?: India and China held senior military commander-level talks in the eastern sector on September 6 and 7 amid continuing tensions in the Taksing area of Arunachal Pradesh.
Why does it matter?: The talks concern military communication and management of tensions along the India-China border, an area with implications for border security and bilateral relations.

Event: Government considers review of GST on UPI merchant fees
Key actors: Government of India; GST Council; retailers; banking and trader associations
What happened?: The government said it hoped the GST Council would review the 18% tax applied to merchant discount rates for UPI transactions after concerns about new fees on large merchant payments.
Why does it matter?: The issue connects tax policy, digital payments, merchant costs and consumer pricing, while the government considers how to maintain acceptance of UPI.

Event: India and Pakistan exchange protests after naval collision
Key actors: Indian Navy; Pakistan Navy; Government of India; Government of Pakistan
What happened?: India and Pakistan summoned each other's diplomats after an Indian and Pakistani naval vessel collided in international waters. Both governments issued strong protests and gave different accounts of the incident.
Why does it matter?: The incident created a new point of military and diplomatic friction between two nuclear-armed neighbours.

Event: India hosts BRICS Leaders' Summit amid geopolitical tensions
Key actors: Government of India; BRICS member states
What happened?: India hosted the BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi on September 12–13 amid tensions surrounding the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran and divisions among BRICS members over the regional crisis.
Why does it matter?: The summit placed India at the centre of multilateral discussions involving major emerging economies and competing positions on regional security and global economic issues.

Event: India receives FDI proposals under revised land-border investment rules
Key actors: Government of India; foreign investors; investors from land-bordering countries
What happened?: India received 29 FDI proposals worth about $511.5 million under a revised policy allowing investors from countries sharing a land border with India to hold non-controlling stakes of up to 10% through the automatic route, subject to applicable conditions.
Why does it matter?: The policy affects foreign investment screening, supply-chain participation and India's approach to investment from neighbouring countries, including China.

Event: RBI forward dollar liabilities reach record level
Key actors: Reserve Bank of India; Indian banks; foreign investors
What happened?: The RBI's net forward dollar liabilities reached a record $200 billion in August after large dollar inflows following temporary policy measures. The RBI began using dollar-rupee swaps to manage the forward position and excess rupee liquidity.
Why does it matter?: The development concerns India's foreign-exchange management, liquidity conditions, reserves and the central bank's response to large capital flows.

Event: India reviews pre-shipment inspection rules for scrap-metal imports
Key actors: DGFT; Material Recycling Association of India; Indian recyclers
What happened?: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade said India had not decided whether to discontinue pre-shipment inspection requirements for imported metal scrap and was reviewing a proposal from recyclers to ease compliance requirements.
Why does it matter?: The rules affect import compliance, recycling-sector supply chains, inspection requirements and the movement of recyclable metal into India.

Event: Election Commission orders review of voter-roll software
Key actors: Election Commission of India; election commissioners; political parties
What happened?: The Election Commission ordered a review of its voter-roll software after a report raised questions about changes to voter lists. The Commission said a committee including an independent technology expert would examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules.
Why does it matter?: The review concerns the administration and verification of electoral rolls and the institutional processes used to maintain voter information.

Event: Severe floods and landslides in northern India
Key actors: State governments; disaster-management authorities; local administrations
What happened?: Heavy rainfall caused flooding and landslides in northern India. In Uttar Pradesh, authorities reported 56 deaths, 46 injuries and damage to more than 1,000 houses. Rescue, relief and damage-assessment operations were underway.
Why does it matter?: Large-scale flooding can place pressure on public infrastructure, emergency-response systems, local administration and government relief capacity.

Event: Tata Trusts propose restructuring of Tata Sons
Key actors: Tata Trusts; Tata Sons; Reserve Bank of India
What happened?: Tata Trusts proposed merging two group entities with Tata Sons in a restructuring that could affect the company's obligation to pursue a public listing under RBI rules. The proposal requires approval from Tata Sons and the RBI.
Why does it matter?: The dispute involves corporate governance, financial regulation and the relationship between a major Indian business group and its regulators.

Event: SEBI expands foreign investor access to commodity derivatives
Key actors: SEBI; foreign investors; portfolio managers
What happened?: SEBI allowed foreign investors to participate in physically settled non-farm commodity contracts and allowed India-based portfolio managers to manage global assets and invest in overseas and to-be-listed securities.
Why does it matter?: The changes affect foreign investor participation, financial-market liquidity and India's efforts to integrate its capital markets with global markets.

Event: SEBI proposes changes to board rules for market institutions
Key actors: SEBI; stock exchanges; clearing corporations; depositories
What happened?: SEBI proposed easing eligibility restrictions for directors of stock exchanges and other market institutions and proposed clearer requirements for senior technology, cybersecurity, compliance and risk officials.
Why does it matter?: The proposals concern governance standards and institutional capacity in India's financial-market infrastructure.

Event: India proposes long-term steel capacity and raw-material strategy
Key actors: Ministry of Steel; Indian steel producers; government
What happened?: India outlined a proposed 20-year steel policy targeting 600 million tonnes of steelmaking capacity by 2047, alongside plans to secure iron ore and coking coal supplies and reduce sector emissions.
Why does it matter?: The policy links industrial capacity, strategic raw-material security, trade exposure and India's long-term manufacturing strategy.

Event: India raises concerns with US over Russia sanctions legislation
Sub-category: India-US relations / Russia sanctions / Foreign policy
Key actors: Government of India; S. Jaishankar; US State Department
What happened?: India's Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar said he reiterated India's concerns to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding proposed US legislation concerning sanctions on Russia and Iran.
Why does it matter?: The issue affects India's relations with the United States and its wider diplomatic and energy relationships involving Russia.

Event: Rupee faces pressure from global oil and financial-market conditions
Key actors: Reserve Bank of India; foreign investors; Indian financial markets
What happened?: The Indian rupee declined during September and the July-September quarter amid high crude-oil prices and global bond-yield pressures, while RBI intervention helped limit the currency's decline.
Why does it matter?: Exchange-rate pressure can affect imported inflation, external balances, financial conditions and the central bank's policy choices.

Event: India intensifies food-safety enforcement
Key actors: FSSAI; state food-safety authorities; food companies
What happened?: Indian food-safety authorities intensified enforcement against misleading labels, altered expiry dates and hygiene violations, while proposed front-of-pack warning labels faced industry and legal resistance.
Why does it matter?: The development concerns regulatory enforcement, consumer protection and the ability of regulators to oversee a rapidly changing food industry.

Event: Jammu and Kashmir Assembly debates restoration of statehood
Key actors: Jammu and Kashmir Assembly; Omar Abdullah; BJP MLAs
What happened?: The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly passed a resolution calling for the restoration of full statehood, leading to disruption and protests by BJP legislators inside the Assembly.
Why does it matter?: The issue concerns relations between the Union government and the J&K administration and continuing political contestation over the region's governance structure.

Event: India reviews foreign-exchange forward liabilities
Key actors: Reserve Bank of India; Indian banks; foreign investors
What happened?: The RBI's net forward dollar liabilities reached a record $200 billion in August. The central bank began using dollar-rupee swaps while managing excess rupee liquidity and its foreign-exchange position.
Why does it matter?: The development concerns India's foreign-exchange management, liquidity conditions, reserves and the RBI's response to large capital flows.
